comparison: Both strongly support the phosphoproteomic approach for identifying CDPK1 substrates (C3, C28-C33). OpenEval emphasizes experimental controls and statistical rigor, while peer reviewers praised the 'state-of-the-art approaches' and 'logical analysis pathways.' High agreement on methodology and findings.

Both support the thiophosphorylation/chemical probe approach (C56, C51-C55). OpenEval details the SILAC labeling and G128M mutant validation, while Reviewer 1 explicitly praised the 'complementary approaches using a chemical probe (KTPyS)' as providing 'paradigms' for substrate identification. Complete agreement.

Both strongly support the identification and characterization of the HOOK complex (C4, C6, C71-C72, C81-C83, C85, C105). OpenEval notes the reciprocal IP-MS evidence and reasonable inference about multiple complexes. Reviewer 1 stated the HOOK complex was 'clearly demonstrated' and Reviewer 2 noted successful determination of this CDPK1 signaling branch. Full agreement.

Both support the live microscopy data on microneme trafficking (C7, C93-C97, C122). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of the CLAMP-mNG marker experiments and differential effects of CDPK1 vs HOOK perturbations. Reviewer 3 explicitly affirmed that CDPK1 activity is required for calcium-stimulated microneme trafficking. Strong agreement.

Both support the functional link between HOOK complex and invasion/microneme exocytosis (C8, C106). OpenEval emphasizes consistency across multiple experimental approaches. Reviewers 1 and 2 both affirmed the HOOK complex role in invasion via microneme trafficking. Complete agreement on primary functional findings.

Both support the myristoylation experiments and functional effects (C38-C45, C103). OpenEval notes the mechanistic link is somewhat inferential. Reviewer 2 mentioned myristoylation as part of the multipronged approach, and no concerns were raised. Agreement, though OpenEval provides more nuanced assessment of mechanistic certainty.

Both support the identification of known motility-related proteins among CDPK1 targets (C62-C70, C104). OpenEval notes these primarily represent literature review/annotation rather than new findings. Reviewer 1 treated this as validation of the approach. Agreement on support, with OpenEval distinguishing validation from novel discovery.

Both support the identification of CDPK1-independent phosphorylation events (C34-C37). OpenEval notes these reveal signaling network complexity and represent secondary observations. Reviewer 1 implicitly accepted this as part of the logical analysis approach. Agreement on findings.

Both support the functional characterization of HOOK and FTS depletion phenotypes (C73-C80). OpenEval details the thorough phenotypic characterization with controls. Peer reviewers accepted the characterization without critique, with Reviewer 1 noting it provided validation. Strong agreement.

Both support the parallel phenotypes of HOOK and FTS (C84, C86-C89). OpenEval emphasizes this provides strong evidence they function in the same pathway. Peer reviewers accepted the functional characterization without concerns. Agreement on same-pathway interpretation.

Both support the expansion microscopy findings (C98-C102). OpenEval notes the unchanged microneme-microtubule distance is well-documented but the inference about unknown factors (C102) is speculative. Peer reviewers described this as 'circumstantial evidence' (Reviewer 3) but accepted the findings. Agreement with similar caution about mechanistic interpretation.

Both support the proximity labeling data (C90-C92). OpenEval emphasizes TurboID provides independent validation of HOOK complex composition. Reviewer 2 explicitly mentioned proximity-based labeling as one of the approaches. Agreement on methodology and findings.

Both address differential effects on egress vs invasion and mechanistic models (C79, C131-C132). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting significant inference beyond direct data and need for additional validation. Peer reviewers accepted the differential effects without challenge, with Reviewer 3 noting 'circumstantial evidence.' Peer reviewers more accepting of speculative interpretations than OpenEval.

OpenEval supports the IP-MS data on myristoylation-dependent protein interactions (C46-C49), noting differential associations suggest myristoylation influences CDPK1 interactions though functional significance remains unclear. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found for these interaction data.

OpenEval notes that background/context claims (C1-C2, C9-C27) represent established knowledge with appropriate citations. These provide necessary context but are not new findings. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate background claims.

OpenEval addresses methodological context and established methods (C5, C50-C55, C107-C108) as supported by citations. Peer Reviewer 1 praised the chemical probe methodology (overlapping C51-C55). Partial overlap with peer review focusing on novel application rather than established methods.

OpenEval rates speculative claims and hypotheses (C109-C112, C124-C127, C130, C135, C143) as UNCERTAIN, noting they extend beyond direct experimental evidence and require additional validation. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate speculative discussion points, generally accepting the overall narrative.

OpenEval supports claims integrating current findings with prior research (C113-C121, C128-C129, C133-C134, C136-C137, C139-C141, C144-C145), noting these represent synthesis rather than new experimental findings. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate synthesis/integration claims.
